newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia's Samper told, yet again, to step down.
newsitem.headline: Colombia's Samper told, yet again, to step down.

text.p: A second leading Colombian newspaper called on President Ernesto Samper on Friday to resign for the good of his country.

El Colombiano of Medellin, the country's second-largest newspaper, said Colombians had endured Samper's "incompetence" long enough and his departure was the only solution to the country's woes. "Colombia today is a nation divided where violence and conflicts of all kind are cropping up in daily life and in the home," it said in an editorial.
On Thursday, Bogota's El Espectador newspaper described Samper as "an unburied corpse" and said his leadership, or lack of it, had brought Colombia to "the brink of an abyss."

Both newspapers urged Samper to resign on several occasions last year, at the height of the political crisis sparked by charges that he used millions of dollars in drug money to finance his 1994 election campaign.
El Colombiano said Colombia would remain on a U.S. blacklist of countries that have failed to cooperate in the war on drugs as long as Samper remains in office.

Last year, U.S. President Bill Clinton "decertified" Colombia and cut U.S. economic aid to the country, a move many Colombians largely blamed on Samper's drug-tainted image. Decertification for a second consecutive year could trigger punitive U.S. commercial sanctions that Clinton stopped short of imposing last year.
